body: will i get a fix, or should i reinstall hermes

Reinstall is the fix here — this is an environment breakage on your box, not a defect in the install path.

`uv trampoline failed to spawn Python child process / Caused by: entity not found (os error 2)` means the `hermes.exe` launcher is still on your PATH but the Python interpreter it points at — `venv\Scripts\python.exe` inside the Hermes install — no longer exists (deleted, moved, or a half-finished/partial install). On a clean PowerShell-installer run, `hermes.exe` references the venv's own python sitting right next to it, so nothing we ship can orphan it; once that interpreter is gone the venv is gone, and a reinstall is the only recovery.

Two things worth noting from the report:
- Install method is listed as "curl | bash" on Windows 11, but our `install.sh` hard-refuses on Windows and tells you to use the PowerShell installer — so that path never produced a working install. Use the PowerShell one-liner below.
- This is the same root cause already triaged in #54979 and #48763 (both closed as cannot-reproduce).

**Recommended — clean reinstall (PowerShell):**

```powershell
cd $env:USERPROFILE
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes
iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)
```

The `cd $env:USERPROFILE` first matters — Windows refuses to delete a directory any shell is `cd`'d inside, and `-Recurse -Force` can leave a broken skeleton behind otherwise.

**If you'd rather repair in place** (the install tree is still there, just the venv is broken):

```powershell
cd $env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force venv,.venv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\uv.exe" venv venv --python 3.11
$env:UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent\venv"
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\uv.exe" pip install -e .
```

Closing as cannot-reproduce, consistent with #54979/#48763. If a fresh `install.ps1` run on your machine ends with a broken `hermes.exe` whose interpreter points anywhere other than `venv\Scripts\python.exe`, please reopen with the full installer log and we'll dig in.
